planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in part shade to full sun; Leucocarpa is a white-fruited sport of Japanese beautyberry that forms dense rings of milky-white berries instead of the species' violet-purple, glowing against bare stems after fall leaf drop.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in part shade to full sun. Leucocarpa is a naturally occurring white-fruited form of Japanese beautyberry, replacing the species' signature violet-purple berry clusters with clean, porcelain-white fruit held in tight rings along gracefully arching branches from late summer into winter. The pale fruit shows up strongly against the plant's own yellowing fall foliage and again after leaf drop, making it a favorite for winter interest and for pairing with the purple-fruited species or with 'Early Amethyst' dichotoma in mixed borders. Like other Japanese beautyberries it flowers and fruits on the current season's wood, so an annual hard pruning in late winter keeps the plant compact and maximizes fruit set. Best fruiting occurs with several hours of direct sun; deep shade reduces berry production.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in part shade to full sun; Albibaccata is a soft pink-fruited selection of Japanese beautyberry, a subtler alternative to the species' bright violet-purple fall display.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in part shade to full sun. Albibaccata is a pale pink-fruited form of Japanese beautyberry, bearing clusters of soft blush-pink berries in place of the species' typical violet-purple, a muted, pastel counterpoint that blends easily with white- and purple-fruited beautyberries in the same planting. Small pink summer flowers give way to the pink fruit in early fall, and light yellow foliage in autumn again sets off the berries before they persist into winter for browsing songbirds. It responds well to an annual hard pruning in late winter since flowering and fruiting occur on new growth each year, and it stays more compact and refined than American beautyberry, suiting foundation plantings and smaller borders. Provide at least half a day of sun for the fullest fruit set.
